newsitem.title: USA: Stock index futures boost March fund returns.
newsitem.headline: Stock index futures boost March fund returns.

text.p: Futures fund managers who traded in the financial markets rather than the commodity markets realized the best returns in the month of March, according to fund performance monitor TASS Management Ltd.
Many of the top peforming managers for the month earned most of their trading gains by shorting U.S. stock index and bond futures contracts, TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
The S&P500 stock index lost nine percent from its value from its record high of 817.68 on February 19 to its intraday low April 4 at 744.04.
But some profits were also made on long positions in the grains markets such as soybeans and soymeal, and long positions in base metals markets also paid off, she said.
"March was a respectable month for futures traders, but peformance wasn't nearly as good as it had been in either January or February," Meaden said.
But for the first time in six months profits from trading foreign exchange futures did not contribute substantially to the performance of the top 10 managers for the month.
After reaching a three year high against the mark and a four year high against the yen in early March, the dollar drifted lower for most of March.
The TASS monthly report follows the peformance of 70 futures and currency managers, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which tracks about 1,600 alternative investment managers and funds globally who manage about $9 billion in assets.
"Alternative" investments programs include hedge funds, Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), managed currency programs, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
